A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same parametrized random-walk clustering research, despite the changed title and substantial revision. Text, equations, tables, figures and all appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian-mixture clustering experiments, benchmark results and alternative vertex-measure and parameter-selection experiments in Section 6 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results, synthetic directed-graph experiments, runtime measurements and extensive sensitivity analyses in Section 4 and Appendices C–D.

M1.justification: The basic P-RW operator is algebraically retained, but the clustering procedure changes substantially. v2 replaces CH/DCH-based diffusion-time selection with an entropy-elbow criterion, adds sampled entropy estimation and random-projection embeddings, and clusters unnormalized operator rows instead of v1's column-normalized kernel rows. Its degree-mixture vertex measure replaces the iterated-flow family, while overlapping a special case already present in v1 Appendix A.3.

E1.justification: Nine point-cloud datasets and Political Blogs are retained. Parkinson, Breast Tissue, Cora, College Football and Karate Club disappear; Olivetti and Email Eu are added. v1's multiscale Gaussian experiment is replaced by directed stochastic block models with baseline, chain and core-periphery structures, substantially changing the tested graph environments.

E2.justification: The scored comparisons in v2 Tables 2–3 add Hermitian-SC, Herm-RW, Simple-Herm, DD-Sym, GSC, PR-PIC and S-PIC, while v1's DI-SIM variants and RSC disappear. Symmetrized spectral clustering remains in revised form as Sym-SC. DSC+ also changes implementation: v1 uses a teleportation extension, whereas v2 Appendix B.2 uses the natural walk's stationary distribution or a long-time approximation.

E3.justification: Evaluation changes from NMI to AMI with PRB aggregation. v1's main benchmarks use ground-truth-based parameter searches, with separate CH/DCH experiments; v2 uses entropy-selected times and shared square-root-of-N projection dimensions across PIC variants. K-NN graph settings also differ: v1 specifies K=floor(log N), whereas v2 Table 5 reports three edges per vertex. New experiments vary graph structure, size and projection settings.

E4.justification: v1's multiscale demonstration and alternative-measure/CH-selection comparisons are replaced by extensive analyses of degree heterogeneity, flow strength, cluster-size imbalance and cluster count. v2 additionally tests vertex-measure parameters, diffusion-time alternatives, entropy sampling, embedding dimension and joint parameter sensitivity, including connectivity-related examinations of Political Blogs and Email Eu.

E5.justification: v1 reports best scores from 100 k-means restarts without uncertainty estimates. v2 Tables 2–3 report means and standard deviations over 100 independent runs, and selected sensitivity experiments explicitly average 50 runs. This substantially changes aggregation and uncertainty reporting; it does not establish an increase in total runs.

E6.justification: v1's NMI tables are replaced by AMI/PRB results under revised methods and settings, so their scores cannot establish same-setting gains or losses. v2 reports equal K-NN PRB scores of 0.96 for ParPIC and S-PIC, and ParPIC AMI of 0.93 on DiSBM Chain. On Email Eu, S-PIC scores 0.49 versus ParPIC's 0.48, qualifying the surrounding superiority claims. Numerous sensitivity and runtime findings are also new.

T1.justification: v2 adds explicit connectivity, aperiodicity and continuity properties for P-RW, parametrized diffusion-map development, and an entropy functional with claimed monotonicity and convergence guarantees and proofs. v1's DCH definition and kernel-centered development are removed or recast. These are substantive formal changes, although Appendix E's Jensen step does not justify the new entropy-monotonicity claim under the stated assumptions.

C1.justification: v1 foregrounds the new diffusion kernel and superiority on most tested datasets. v2 reframes the contribution around reversible power-iteration clustering, entropy-based time selection and low-dimensional computational efficiency. Its abstract specifies weakly connected digraphs and competitive accuracy, while the introduction adds explicit scalability claims, including a dense-graph complexity comparison.

C2.justification: v2 develops a regime-dependent interpretation: directionality provides limited gains on reciprocal K-NN graphs but matters more for asymmetric inter-cluster flows. It adds explanations of degree and cluster-count effects, dataset-dependent parameter sensitivity, failures of positivity at extreme vertex-measure settings, and irregular entropy behavior when graph assumptions fail. These substantially extend v1's general symmetrization and irreducibility discussion.

D1.justification: v2 replaces v1's search-grid and per-result optimal-parameter documentation with detailed baseline constructions, DiSBM generation matrices, projection and probe defaults, KNEEDLE selection, and the acceleration comparator's threshold of 10^-4. It also adds a promise to release code and data upon publication, but supplies no actual access. These are substantial changes to reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Research positioning shifts toward PIC scalability and distinctions between Hermitian, spectral and probabilistic approaches. v2 adds substantial discussion and citations for Hermitian clustering, alternative symmetrizations, adaptive power iteration and entropy-based diffusion selection, while removing much of v1's regularized/co-clustering and metastability coverage. The Sevi et al. 2022/2025 reference is an updated instance of the same cited work, not a new addition.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, methodological narrative and discussion are extensively rewritten. P-RWDKC becomes ParPIC, previously separate theoretical and practical sections are reorganized, and the appendix is rebuilt into notation, implementation, experiments, sensitivity and proof sections. The title and author information also change.

P2.justification: v2 changes the main text to two columns and substantially redesigns the visual presentation. The Gaussian scatterplot disappears; new displays include a pipeline schematic, operator visualizations, runtime and sensitivity curves, and heatmaps. Results tables switch orientation and add uncertainty and PRB displays, alongside new method, notation and dataset-statistics tables.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical validation through matched PIC controls, uncertainty reporting, directed-structure stress tests and extensive sensitivity and runtime analyses. However, it introduces problems in central theoretical and efficiency claims: Appendix E's Jensen step does not establish entropy monotonicity, and the advertised O(N^1.5) dense-graph cost conflicts with the matrix multiplication specified in Equation 8. The empirical benefits are substantial, but their net balance against these new credibility problems is not reliably assessable.
